name: Roman Silver
lede: Roman Silver is a muted blue-grey listed in Ridgway's 1912 color atlas as a silver-metal tone, its exact Roman connection undocumented.

sections.title: A silver with an unexplained adjective
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[deep-plumbago-grey]] and [[grey]], at Why Ridgway called this particular shade "Roman," rather than simply "silver" or another modifier, is not explained in the sources consulted here [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 revision files it as block 203, "bluish gray" [1][2].

In LCH terms the color measures lightness 57, chroma 8, hue 274, placing it between the plainer tone [[silver|Silver]] and [[deep-plumbago-grey|Deep Plumbago Grey]], close to [[warm-silver|Warm Silver]] and to [[light-slate-grey|Light Slate Grey]] elsewhere in the library [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A screen match for this grey-blue appears in 365 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.5 percent, as photographed, nearly three times the archive's average rate in work from the 1930s decade [2]. André Derain, Theodor Philipsen and Claude Monet all carry it well above the archive's base rate, often in overcast skies and shadowed fabric rather than skin [2]. Every figure here is a computed color match on an aged, varnished painting, not a pigment identification [2].
